summary: Branch office HTTP-CONNECT tunnel proxy injects Alt-Svc/HTTP3 causing QUIC fallback and intermittent presigned range fetch failures on private deploy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures when fetching large model shard ranges from S3-backed presigned URLs using a private deployment behind a branch-office HTTP-CONNECT tunneling proxy. The customer's proxy rewrites HTTP responses and is observed injecting Alt-Svc/HTTP3/QUIC hints into 200 responses. Impact: Several tens of range GETs for large shards are returning 403/416/connection reset or large delays, leading to degraded warmup and increased token latency for hosted inference. Impact window appears correlated with branch-office work hours.

Environment: Private deployment (VPCE-connected nodes) in us-east-1, customers use a branch-office HTTP-CONNECT tunneling proxy for egress that performs response header rewriting and an ALPN/alt-svc cache. Customer reports the proxy is managed by their corporate networking team and is not under Redwood control.

Observed behavior: During incidents the client attempts to negotiate HTTP/3 (QUIC) to the S3 endpoint after seeing Alt-Svc. QUIC traffic is either blocked by an upstream firewall or misrouted by the customer's WAN optimizer. QUIC fail leads to connection resets and racey range re-requests, sometimes resulting in presigned host mismatch errors (403) when a follow-up attempt is routed via a different NAT public IP/ALPN mapping.

Expected behavior: The egress proxy should not inject Alt-Svc hints for presigned S3 responses passing through a CONNECT tunnel. Range downloads should remain over the established TCP/TLS channel or correctly fall back without losing auth or range semantics.

Reproducibility: Intermittent but reproducible under customer's branch-office network conditions. We can trigger by forcing large-range downloads from a client behind the proxy while the proxy's alt-svc cache is populated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a host behind customer HTTP-CONNECT tunneling proxy, request a presigned S3 range GET for a large model shard (multi-GB range or multipart range sequence)
2) Observe response headers returned by the proxy to the client (look for Alt-Svc: h3="" or Alt-Svc entries pointing to same host)
3) Watch client network stack: client attempts HTTP/3/QUIC handshake to S3 host after seeing Alt-Svc hint
4) If QUIC is blocked or rewriten mid-handshake by WAN device, note resulting behavior: TCP/TLS reset, 403 presigned host mismatch on re-request, or range reassembly failures (416)
logs: Client-side quic log: connection failed: 0x2 (version_negotiation) after 62ms
Client retry via TCP: GET range -> 403 Forbidden (signature mismatch: request seen from different egress IP)
investigation_notes: Initial triage: reproduced by engineering using customer-provided proxy VM image; proxy rewrites and injects Alt-Svc headers into CONNECT responses for caching/optimization reasons.

Network tracing: QUIC packets were sent but dropped by customer WAN optimizer; TCP fallback attempts performed but some retries used a different NAT mapping leading to presigned signature mismatch (403)

Serving runtime: no evidence of shard corruption on Redwood side; S3 logs show multiple short-lived QUIC SYN-like attempts followed by aborted GETs, then a small number of valid GETs that returned 403 due to signature mismatch (client IP changed)

Hypothesis: Proxy's Alt-Svc injection plus asymmetric NAT/NAT64 in branch traffic causes QUIC attempt followed by re-request with different source address/port, invalidating presigned URL signature window and range semantics.

Related: customer uses a corporate transparent proxy that caches Alt-Svc and rewrites host headers for optimization under heavy load; we suspect this optimization is intended for web traffic but breaks signed S3 range fetch semantics when used in CONNECT mode.
comments: Aisha Rahman (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer opened after seeing repeated shard fetch failures during nightly warmup. Provided packet captures and proxy config snippets.
Carlos Mendez (Eng) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed Alt-Svc injection in proxy capture. Spun up test VM and reproduced QUIC handshake attempts followed by NAT translation changes on re-request.
Customer network lead (FinTechCo) - 2026-03-11: We see proxy logic that rewrites 200 responses and adds Alt-Svc for caching. We can toggle off the optimization but need guidance on safe config.
Carlos Mendez (Eng) - 2026-03-12: Requesting customer to disable Alt-Svc injection for any CONNECT tunnel traffic or exclude s3.amazonaws.com prefix. Proposed workaround documented below.
Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-12: Created INT-324 for internal runbook updates to detect Alt-Svc injected into CONNECT flows and add a diagnostic in our private-deploy health checks.
suggested_workaround: Ask customer to disable Alt-Svc/HTTP3 header injection for CONNECT-tunneled responses or add an exception for S3 endpoints / our artifact domain. If disabling globally isn't possible, whitelist presigned hostnames so proxy returns original headers. Alternatively, increase presigned URL enforcement tolerance by issuing presigned URLs bound to egress IP ranges (if acceptable to customer security), or ensure NAT stability for branch egress so retried requests retain same source address.
